title: Embedded beat crashes with AttributeError instead of rejecting a green pool
title_original: Fix Django worker recursion bug + defensive checks for pool_cls.__module__
text_original:
## Description

This PR builds on top of #10045 by @bruunotrindade to add defensive checks for `pool_cls.__module__` access in additional locations throughout the codebase.

### Root Cause (from #10045)

`DjangoWorkerFixup.__init__` was creating a `WorkController` instance via the `worker` or `WorkController(app)` pattern. This created a circular dependency where:

- `WorkController.__init__` triggers the `worker_init` signal
- `DjangoFixup.on_worker_init` creates/accesses `DjangoWorkerFixup`
- `DjangoWorkerFixup.__init__` tries to create another `WorkController`
- Infinite recursion ensues

Additionally, `pool_cls` can be a string (e.g., `'prefork'`, `'solo'`, `'gevent'`) instead of a class object, which causes `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__module__'` when trying to access `pool_cls.__module__`.

### Changes in this PR

This PR includes all changes from #10045 plus:

1. **`celery/contrib/testing/worker.py`**: Added defensive check for `pool_cls` being a string in `TestWorkController.__init__`

2. **`celery/worker/components.py`**: Added defensive check for `pool_cls` being a string in `Beat.create`

3. **New unit tests**: Added tests to verify the defensive checks work correctly when `pool_cls` is a string

### Pattern Applied

```python
# Before (can raise AttributeError if pool_cls is a string)
if w.pool_cls.__module__.endswith(('gevent', 'eventlet')):

# After (handles both string and class pool_cls)
pool_module = w.pool_cls if isinstance(w.pool_cls, str) else w.pool_cls.__module__
if pool_module.endswith(('gevent', 'eventlet')):
```

## Testing

- All existing unit tests pass
- Added 2 new tests for `Beat.create` with string pool_cls
- Pre-commit hooks pass (flake8, mypy, isort, etc.)
- Test coverage maintained

## Related Issues

- #10042 - Original issue reporting RecursionError
- #10045 - Original PR by @bruunotrindade fixing the root cause
- #10023 - Previous attempts to fix the issue

## Acknowledgments

Thanks to @bruunotrindade for identifying and fixing the root cause in #10045. This PR extends that fix to cover additional edge cases.
text_rewritten: Starting a worker with an embedded beat on a green (eventlet/gevent) pool used to fail with a clear configuration error telling you to run beat standalone. When the pool is given by name on the command line instead of as an already-resolved class, the same start-up now dies with "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__module__'" -- the guard reads module metadata off what is just a plain string. Pool selection can legitimately arrive either way, and the guard has to recognise a green pool in both forms. Pools that are not green must keep starting normally when named the same way.
body: Starting a worker with an embedded beat on a green (eventlet/gevent) pool used to fail with a clear configuration error telling you to run beat standalone. When the pool is given by name on the command line instead of as an already-resolved class, the same start-up now dies with "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__module__'" -- the guard reads module metadata off what is just a plain string. Pool selection can legitimately arrive either way, and the guard has to recognise a green pool in both forms. Pools that are not green must keep starting normally when named the same way.
acceptance_hint: Creating the embedded-beat bootstep against a green pool raises the configuration error whether the pool arrives as the string 'gevent'/'eventlet' or as a class, while a non-green pool name still builds the embedded service.
